Insertion sort, step by step

Insertion sort grows a sorted part at the front of the array. It takes the next value and swaps it left past every larger value until it is in order, the way many people sort a hand of cards.

Click the figure, then use ← →, space, Home and End, or the buttons.

How it works

  1. The first value alone is sorted.
  2. Take the next value.
  3. While the value to its left is larger, swap them.
  4. Repeat until every value has been inserted.

Cost

Time
O(n²) on average and in the worst case. O(n) on input that is already nearly sorted.
Space
O(1): it sorts in place.
Stable
Yes: equal values keep their order.

The code behind this figure

Nothing here is hand-animated. The figure comes from this code: a plain insertion sort with stepthru tracer calls, such as compare and swap, that record each step.
